attempted_claim: Fix odd n=2m+1>=3 and s in (1/2,1). Let ((CP^1)^n, omega_mon) with each factor of area 1 and let Theta^n_s be the Chekanov-type Lagrangian torus of Vianna, Definition 4.2 (fiber of f=prod x_i/y_i over gamma_s at T^{n-1}-moment 0, with int_beta omega=s). Is Theta^n_s Hamiltonian displaceable? I.e. either construct Psi in Ham((CP^1)^n) with Psi(Theta^n_s) cap Theta^n_s = empty, or prove Theta^n_s is non-displaceable via non-vanishing (bulk-deformed) Lagrangian Floer cohomology HF(Theta^n_s,(b,b_vec);Lambda_{0,nov}) cong H^*(Theta^n_s;Lambda_{0,nov}) for some bulk b and weak bounding cochain b_vec.
decisive_failure: originality: Fails: Vianna Lemma 5.3 already records val(u)!=1/2 iff n=2m balanced-sign, whose contrapositive is exactly odd-n val(u)=1/2 for all bulks/patterns. Combined with Vianna u=T^s exp() and Cor 2.8, the HF no-go is mechanically implied. Report mischaracterizes Lemma 5.3 as even-only; full-text inspection shows it covers odd n. Prior need not state headline verbatim; substantive implication defeats novelty. Scalar/bulk-unit extensions are trivial parameter substitutions.
